samples.question: This page shows black slabs, grey decoration and small coloured beads. Only black ink is a wall; grey marks are decoration and never count, even when a coloured bead sits inside a grey outline. Each black slab is a solid block with one or two square holes punched through it, and the white page shows through every hole. A bead is shut inside a pocket when the white area holding that bead is completely surrounded by black ink, so that no white path leads from the bead to the edge of the page without stepping on black ink. A channel cut clean through the wall of a hole joins that hole to the white space outside its slab, so a bead in a hole with such a channel is not shut inside a pocket. Beads lying on the open page, beads inside grey outlines, and holes that hold no bead never count. How big the slabs are, where they sit on the page, how many holes the page shows in total, how many beads the page shows and how much ink the page holds never decide the answer. How many beads are shut inside a pocket? Answer with a whole number from 0 to 5.
